parsed.explanation: Combined US/Oklahoma regime presents universal birth-sex document and facility exposure, entry refusal/ineligibility risk, and birth-sex custody with hormone withdrawal and documented abuse, without execution or routine police sweeps. Functioning courts have enjoined some measures, private care remains available, and national hate-crime/employment protections exist, but Oklahoma adds K-12 facility bans, document foreclosure, public-care bans for minors and adults, and no state anti-discrimination or hate-crime cover. Consequences if outed centre on exclusion, detention, custody harm and care denial, mitigated only partially by litigation.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal passports/visas only M/F matching birth sex; X stopped; document discrepancy triggers refusal, extra evidence, possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; reported confiscations/stranding.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; passport policy challenged by ACLU and allowed by Supreme Court in Nov 2025, so litigation is live but not protective currently.
entry_documents.interaction: Home passport mismatch at entry interacts with state K-12/facility and custody rules if detained, compounding refusal into detention exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National prisons adopted conversion practices including hair cutting, hormone removal, psychiatric drugs; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse; placement by birth sex implied by binary order.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Courts have blocked/enjoined some orders; no documented remedy specifically restoring hormones or placement for visitors; bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry fraud allegation or facility trespass can lead to detention where birth-sex placement and care denial apply.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal binary order bars government single-sex facilities congruent with identity; Oklahoma SB615/EO bans K-12 and state-owned facilities by birth sex; neighbouring-state trespass arrest shows criminal enforcement direction.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Nationally some bans are government-only and have exemptions; Oklahoma tracker specifies K-12; no state protection for gender identity.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal and state bans overlap in schools, capitol and public buildings, leaving no identity-congruent public option despite private alternatives.

care_services.exposure: SB904 (2026) bans public funds, Medicaid and state facilities for gender-affirming care for minors and adults; employee violations are a misdemeanor; minor care already banned.
care_services.protection: Private facilities with private insurance/out-of-pocket remain; exemptions for counselling, emergency, intersex and complications; some national orders enjoined.
care_services.interaction: Adult visitor may obtain care privately, but emergency/hospital ward placement and public clinic access remain birth-sex based.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders define sex at birth, purge gender-ideology materials, investigate schools/teachers for pronoun use, and counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups; public support for birth-sex documents is high.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; US courts enjoined several orders; marriage and Bostock employment ruling remain nationally.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing raises police/school scrutiny and social hostility, while court injunctions create uneven, time-sensitive enforcement.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor cannot access gender-affirming care in public/state facilities, must use birth-sex school facilities/sports, and teachers face investigation for social transition support; guardian may face costs/private-only access.
minors_guardians.protection: Emergency treatment and mental-health counselling exempted; private care and parental private payment not criminalised for patients.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling family faces combined school-facility, sports, document and public-care restrictions, with federal minor-care orders also litigated.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2018 death threats against trans student and Nex Benedict 2024 death after bathroom beating are resident cases, not visitor incidents; no state hate-crime cover for gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime prosecution available; one Oklahoma city bans discrimination in employment/housing/public accommodations, three only for city employment.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: No documented visitor-specific violence pattern; absence in thin local record is not safety, especially with hostile official framing.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: HB1225 signature unknown, licence-marker status not documented, specific July 2026 traveller grade not stated, and several orders are in flux, making timing uncertain.
remedies_unknowns.protection: ACLU passport suit, challenges to executive orders, and Oklahoma birth-certificate litigation show courts can grant relief, though outcomes slow and partial.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation uncertainty does not cure operative federal/state exposures at entry, facilities or custody during travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar universal exclusion without routine imprisonment: here entry refusal, document mismatch and facility bans are routine, but custody abuse and possible lifetime ineligibility make it at least as severe, offset partially by active courts.

Higher than 0.55: 0.55 is mainly secondary screening and administrative refusal with remedies; this case adds birth-sex custody with hormone removal/abuse, state facility criminalisation nearby, and public-care bans.

Higher than 0.25: 0.25 has birth-sex prison assaults with slow remedies and frequent custody; here imprisonment for presentation is not typical, private care exists, and national courts have blocked some measures.

Well below 0.65: 0.65 has working ombuds remedies reversing refusals within hours; here remedies are litigated, slow and often unavailable in custody/facilities, with no visitor-specific ombuds documented.

parsed.synthesis: Operative interaction is entry/document discrepancy to possible refusal or fraud referral, then facility exclusion by birth sex, then, if detained, birth-sex custody and hormone interruption; for minors, public care and school access are also barred. Protections are real but external to the encounter: federal hate-crime/employment law, private care, one protective city, and courts blocking some orders. They do not pre-empt federal entry, federal facilities, or state school/public-facility enforcement. Hence elevated-to-high risk, above organised-targeting/imprisonment regimes but materially below jurisdictions where document/facility/custody exposures are absent or promptly remedied.
